filename: Efficient Emulation, Uncertainty Quantification, and Sensitivity Analysis for a Land Surface Model using Evidential Deep Learning.pdf
title: Efficient Emulation, Uncertainty Quantification, and Sensitivity Analysis for a Land Surface Model using Evidential Deep Learning
venue: Earth and Space Science Open Archive (essoar)
code_availability: All scripts used to preprocess data, train and evaluate the evidential deep neural network (EDNN) emulator, perform uncertainty quantification, and conduct sensitivity analyses are archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17418678 (Silwimba, 2025). The evidential model was implemented using the MILES-GUESS package (Schreck et al., 2024).
testbed_rationale: The paper provides a publicly accessible dataset on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.15170936) representing a 500-member perturbed parameter ensemble from CLM5 alongside archived open source code on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.17418678). This provides an ideal benchmark/testbed for land surface model emulation, uncertainty quantification, and sensitivity analysis.
pain_points: Extreme value compression: EDNN exhibits minor regression toward the mean, underpredicting extreme high positive LAI anomalies and damping extreme negative anomalies

Spring phenological transition error: Low true variance in spring LAI leads to lower explained variance (R^2 = 0.26) despite strong skill score (0.71), and onset timing error can spike by 2-4 months during anomalous springs
Under-dispersion at distribution tails in the evidential predictive distribution as indicated by PIT histograms
High computational cost of running full LSM PPEs (such as CLM5) at scale, motivating surrogate emulation
Structural model bias inheritance: The emulator cannot correct underlying CLM5 structural errors/missing processes (e.g., disturbance/fire)
extraction_notes: Author list combines the author order from the title page and the main text; the order matches the main text header (p. 1 of manuscript). The work is funded in part by NSF LEAP STC (award 2019625-STC to author LH).
